title: Platformer 2D: scenes, nodes and signals
intro: You will be able to trace how Platformer 2D is assembled from instanced scenes (Game, Level, Player, PauseMenu), follow a coin pickup from Coin to the HUD counter through signals, and explain how the same Player and Level scenes are reused for singleplayer and splitscreen.
subject: How this platformer is structured: scenes, nodes and signals
domainGap: I know Unity but not Godot
materialNote: Docs gap: README.md mentions a default game.tscn and a src/level/ folder, but the project runs game_singleplayer.tscn (project.godot) and level/ is at the root. It also never mentions splitscreen mode or the signal wiring.
docsNote: The README refers to a default game.tscn and a src/level/ folder that do not exist here (the main scene is game_singleplayer.tscn and level/ is at the root), and it does not explain the Game/Level/Player/PauseMenu composition.

chapters.title: Game scenes: Level, Player and the interface layer
chapters.goal: Explain how game_singleplayer.tscn composes Level, Player and PauseMenu by instancing, what game.gd (class Game) does as the root script, and why the project autoloads Music from music.tscn.
chapters.hootIntro: Platformer 2D is a handful of scenes stacked like blocks: game_singleplayer.tscn instances Level, Player and a PauseMenu, and game.gd keeps watch over them.

steps.title: The entry point: game_singleplayer.tscn
steps.body: `project.godot` sets `run/main_scene` to `res://game_singleplayer.tscn`, so that scene is what runs on Play. Its root is a plain `Node` named `Game` with `game.gd` attached. Everything else is a child, and most children are **instances of other scenes** (`level/level.tscn`, `player/player.tscn`, `gui/pause_menu_singleplayer.tscn`), not nodes defined inline. The folders mirror that: `player/`, `level/`, `enemy/`, `gui/` each own a scene plus its script and assets.

steps.title: Scene instancing, Unity-prefab style
steps.concept: In Godot a scene is a reusable tree of nodes saved to a .tscn file; instancing it inside another scene is close to nesting a prefab in Unity, and the instance can override properties locally.
steps.applied: In `game_singleplayer.tscn`, `Level` is an instance of `level.tscn` (line 12) and `Player` is an instance of `player.tscn` parented under `Level` (line 14). The instance then overrides `z_index`, `position` and `scale` (lines 15-17), much like a prefab instance override, without touching `player.tscn` itself.

steps.title: The singleplayer node tree
steps.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Game["Game (Node, game.gd)"]
  Level["Level (instance of level/level.tscn)"]
  Player["Player (instance of player/player.tscn)"]
  IL["InterfaceLayer (CanvasLayer, layer 100)"]
  PM["PauseMenu (instance of gui/pause_menu_singleplayer.tscn)"]
  Game --> Level
  Level --> Player
  Game --> IL
  IL --> PM
steps.caption: Game owns the world (Level, with Player inside) and a CanvasLayer at layer 100 for the UI. Boxes marked (instance) come from separate .tscn files.

stops.annotation: `class_name Game` registers a global type; `@onready` fetches the PauseMenu by path `InterfaceLayer/PauseMenu` once the tree is ready. The splitscreen script later does `extends Game`.
Fullscreen toggle runs in `_unhandled_input`, so it only fires if no UI consumed the event. `set_input_as_handled()` stops it propagating.
Pause flips `tree.paused` and calls `PauseMenu.open()` or `close()`. This works while paused only because the scene sets `process_mode = 3` (Always) on the Game root, see `game_singleplayer.tscn:9`.

steps.title: Why Game keeps running while paused
steps.prompt: Click the line that lets the Game root keep receiving input while the tree is paused.
steps.explanation: `process_mode = 3` is PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS. Without it, `Game._unhandled_input` would stop firing once `tree.paused` is true, and `toggle_pause` could never unpause. The Level and Player inherit the default and freeze.

takeaways: `game_singleplayer.tscn` is the main scene: a `Game` root (game.gd) that instances `Level`, `Player` (inside Level) and a `PauseMenu` under a CanvasLayer at layer 100.
`Game._unhandled_input` handles fullscreen and pause, and relies on `process_mode = 3` on the root so it still runs while the tree is paused.
`Music` (music.tscn) is an autoload in project.godot, so it outlives the scene swaps done by PauseMenu.

chapters.title: Signals in practice: from Coin to the pause menu counter
chapters.goal: Trace coin_collected from Coin._on_body_entered through Player's signal and the connection in game_singleplayer.tscn to PauseMenu._on_coin_collected and CoinsCounter.collect_coin, and tell editor-wired connections from code calls.

chapters.title: One Player scene, two modes: splitscreen reuse
chapters.goal: Explain how game_splitscreen.tscn and game_splitscreen.gd extend Game, reuse player.tscn with action_suffix _p1/_p2, share one world_2d between two SubViewports, and how both players feed the same PauseMenu signal.
